text.p: Following are the highlights of the main stories in Croatian newspapers on Thursday. Reuters has not verified them and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- Croatia cannot withdraw its troops from the border with the Federal Republic of Yugoslavia unless Yugoslav troops do the same, says Foreign Ministry spokesman Zeljko Trkanjac in response to the latest proposal by the U.N. administrator in Eastern Slavonia Jacques Klein during talks in Belgrade.
- First five Croatian refugees from Eastern Slavonia officially returned to their home towns of Ilok and Bilje on Wednesday after almost six years of exile.

- Prime Minister Zlatko Matesa received a business delegation from Indonesia which expressed interest in cooperation in industry, shipbuilding, science and technology. Indonesia might use Croatia as a springoboard to central European markets, the prime minister said.
- Initial data indicate that turnover from tourism may be 30 percent higher than in 1996, Tourism Minister Niko Bulic said.
- The birth rate in Croatia was higher than the death rate for the first time since 1990 with 53,811 newborns against 50,636 dead, according to state statistics.

- British building materials group RMC which has a controlling stake in Croatia's cement producer Dalmacijacement injected more than 160 million German marks to upgrade its technology in the biggest foreign investment in Croatia so far.
- The government will purchase the entire surplus of wheat crops estimated at 420,000 tonnes at a favouirable price of 1.10 kuna per kilo, Agriculture Ministry official Vlado Bicanic said.
- Shipper Jadrolinija to introduce 17 international ferry routes from mid-July as the peak tourist season gets underway. -- Zagreb Newsroom, 385 1 4557075
